6294-no-defense-volume-3.title: No Defense Volume 3
6294-no-defense-volume-3.creator: Gilbert Parker
6294-no-defense-volume-3.description: A book by Gilbert Parker. e, the cotton-fields, the long ranges of negro houses like thatched cottages, the penguin hedges, with their beautiful red, blue, and white convolvuluses; the lime, logwood, and breadfruit trees, the avocado-pear, the feathery bamboo, and the jack-fruit tree; and between the mountains and his own sugar-estates, negro settlements and pens.

arxiv-2009-11691.title: Experimentally friendly approach towards nonlocal correlations in multisetting N N -partite Bell scenarios
arxiv-2009-11691.creator: Artur Barasiński, Antonín Černoch, Wiesław Laskowski, Karel Lemr, Tamás Vértesi, Jan Soubusta
arxiv-2009-11691.description: Abstract In this work, we study a recently proposed operational measure of nonlocality by Fonseca and Parisio [Phys. Rev. A 92 , 030101(R) (2015)] which describes the probability of violation of local realism under randomly sampled observables, and the strength of such violation as described by resistance to white noise admixture.

arxiv-2101-10859.title: The strong effect of network resolution on electricity system models with high shares of wind and solar
arxiv-2101-10859.creator: Martha Maria Frysztacki, Jonas Hörsch, Veit Hagenmeyer, Tom Brown
arxiv-2101-10859.description: Abstract Energy system modellers typically choose a low spatial resolution for their models based on administrative boundaries such as countries, which eases data collection and reduces computation times. However, a low spatial resolution can lead to sub-optimal investment decisions for wind and solar generation.

arxiv-2105-12307.title: Optimal Transport Based Refinement of Physics-Informed Neural Networks
arxiv-2105-12307.creator: Vaishnav Tadiparthi, Raktim Bhattacharya
arxiv-2105-12307.description: Abstract In this paper, we propose a refinement strategy to the well-known Physics-Informed Neural Networks (PINNs) for solving partial differential equations (PDEs) based on the concept of Optimal Transport (OT). Conventional black-box PINNs solvers have been found to suffer from a host of issues: spectral bias in fully-connected architectures, unstable gradient pathologies, as well as difficulties with convergence and accuracy.

arxiv-2110-15722.title: ICDM 2020 Knowledge Graph Contest: Consumer Event-Cause Extraction
arxiv-2110-15722.creator: Congqing He † \dagger, Jie Zhang † \dagger, Xiangyu Zhu ‡ \ddagger, Huan Liu, Yukun Huang
arxiv-2110-15722.description: Abstract Consumer Event-Cause Extraction, the task aimed at extracting the potential causes behind certain events in the text, has gained much attention in recent years due to its wide applications. The ICDM 2020 conference sets up an evaluation competition that aims to extract events and the causes of the extracted events with a specified subject (a brand or product).

arxiv-2205-13602.title: Consistent and fast inference in compartmental models of epidemics using Poisson Approximate Likelihoods
arxiv-2205-13602.creator: Michael Whitehouse
arxiv-2205-13602.description: A 2022 arXiv research paper by Michael Whitehouse. Addressing the challenge of scaling-up epidemiological inference to complex and heterogeneous models, we introduce Poisson Approximate Likelihood (PAL) methods. In contrast to the popular ODE approach to compartmental modelling, in which a large population limit is used to motivate a deterministic model, PALs are derived from approximate filtering equations for finite-population, stochastic compartmental models, and the large population limit drives consistency of maximum PAL estimators.

arxiv-2209-13853.title: Thinking Hallucination for Video Captioning
arxiv-2209-13853.creator: Nasib Ullah, Partha Pratim Mohanta
arxiv-2209-13853.description: Abstract With the advent of rich visual representations and pre-trained language models, video captioning has seen continuous improvement over time. Despite the performance improvement, video captioning models are prone to hallucination. Hallucination refers to the generation of highly pathological descriptions that are detached from the source material. In video captioning, there are two kinds of hallucination: object and action hallucination.

arxiv-2211-01145.title: Safety-centric and Smart Outdoor Workplace: A New Research Direction and Its Technical Challenges Thanks: Supported in part by Chilean National Research and Development Agency (ANID, Chile) under Grant FONDECYT Iniciación 11180905.
arxiv-2211-01145.creator: Zheng Li 1 [ORCID: 0000-0002-9704-7651] {}^{\texttt{[ORCID: 0000-0002-9704-7651]}}, Mauricio Pradena Miquel 2, Pedro Pinacho-Davidson 1
arxiv-2211-01145.description: A 2022 arXiv research paper by Zheng Li 1 [ORCID: 0000-0002-9704-7651] {}^{\texttt{[ORCID: 0000-0002-9704-7651]}}, Mauricio Pradena Miquel 2, Pedro Pinacho-Davidson 1. Despite the fact that outside is becoming the frontier of indoor workplaces, a large amount of real-world work like road construction has to be done by outdoor human activities in open areas. Given the promise of the smart workplace in various aspects including productivity and safety, we decided to employ smart workplace technologies for a collaborative outdoor project both to improve the work efficiency and to reduce the worker injuries.

arxiv-2302-05193.title: Structural Break Detection in Quantile Predictive Regression Models with Persistent Covariates Thanks: I would like to thank Jose Olmo, Tassos Magdalinos and Jean-Yves Pitarakis for guidance, support and continuous encouragement throughout the PhD programme. Furthermore, this study has been inspired
arxiv-2302-05193.creator: Christis Katsouris
arxiv-2302-05193.description: Abstract We propose an econometric environment for structural break detection in nonstationary quantile predictive regressions. We establish the limit distributions for a class of Wald and fluctuation type statistics based on both the ordinary least squares estimator and the endogenous instrumental regression estimator proposed by Phillips and Magdalinos, 2009 .

arxiv-2404-18042.title: Pose-aware 3D Beamwidth Adaptation for Mobile Extended Reality
arxiv-2404-18042.creator: Alperen Duru 1 , Mohammad Mozaffari 2 , Mehrnaz Afshang 2 , Ticao Zhang 2 , Talha Khan 2 , Todd E. Humphreys 1 , and Jeffrey G. Andrews 1
arxiv-2404-18042.description: Abstract This paper presents a sensor-aided pose-aware beamwidth adaptation design for a conceptual extended reality (XR) Head-Mounted Display (HMD) equipped with a 2D planar array. The beam is tracked and adapted on the user side by leveraging HMD orientation estimates.

A Pisot numeration system U = ( u n ) n ⩾ 0 U=(u_{n})_{n\geqslant 0} for ℕ \mathbb{N} is one where the sequence of positive integers ( u n ) n ⩾ 0 (u_{n})_{n\geqslant 0} , with u n = 1 u_{n}=1 , is generated by a recurrence whose polynomial is the minimal polynomial of a Pisot number.

arxiv-2407-14089.creator: Patrik Knopf, Jonas Stange

arxiv-2411-05231.title: Evaluating GPT-4 at Grading Handwritten Solutions in Math Exams
arxiv-2411-05231.creator: Adriana Caraeni, Alexander Scarlatos, Andrew Lan
arxiv-2411-05231.description: Abstract Recent advances in generative artificial intelligence (AI) have shown promise in accurately grading open-ended student responses. However, few prior works have explored grading handwritten responses due to a lack of data and the challenge of combining visual and textual information.

arxiv-2506-04620.title: A Resource Allocating Compiler for Lattice Surgery
arxiv-2506-04620.creator: Alan Robertson, Haowen Gao, Yuval R. Sanders
arxiv-2506-04620.description: Abstract The emerging field of quantum resource estimation is aimed at providing estimates of the hardware requirements (‘quantum resources’) needed to execute a useful, fault-tolerant quantum computation. Given that quantum computers are intended to compete with supercomputers, useful quantum computations are likely to involve the use of millions of qubits and error correction clock cycles.

arxiv-2508-10164.title: Pruning Long Chain-of-Thought of Large Reasoning Models via Small-Scale Preference Optimization
arxiv-2508-10164.creator: Bin Hong, Jiayu Liu, Zhenya Huang, Kai Zhang, Mengdi Zhang
arxiv-2508-10164.description: Abstract Recent advances in Large Reasoning Models (LRMs) have demonstrated strong performance on complex tasks through long Chain-of-Thought (CoT) reasoning. However, their lengthy outputs increase computational costs and may lead to overthinking, raising challenges in balancing reasoning effectiveness and efficiency. Current methods for efficient reasoning often compromise reasoning quality or require extensive resources.

pmc-10558412.title: Mechanical stress confers nuclear and functional changes in derived leukemia cells from persistent confined migration
pmc-10558412.creator: Ana de Lope-Planelles, Raquel González-Novo, Elena Madrazo, Gracia Peralta-Carrero, María Pilar Cruz Rodríguez, Héctor Zamora-Carreras, Verónica Torrano, Horacio López-Menéndez, Pedro Roda-Navarro, Francisco Monroy, Javier Redondo-Muñoz
pmc-10558412.description: Nuclear deformability plays a critical role in cell migration. During this process, the remodeling of internal components of the nucleus has a direct impact on DNA damage and cell behavior; however, how persistent migration promotes nuclear changes leading to phenotypical and functional consequences remains poorly understood.

pmc-11607540.title: Personalized and adaptive interventions for smoking cessation: Emerging trends and determinants of efficacy
pmc-11607540.creator: Gal Cohen, Carlo Maria Bellanca, Renato Bernardini, Jed E. Rose, Riccardo Polosa
pmc-11607540.description: SummaryCigarette smoking addiction is a leading cause of morbidity and mortality and presents a challenging interventional target. Interventions for stopping smoking offer trade-offs in ability to displace or blunt the effects of cigarettes, which include positive and negative reinforcement, psychological reward, aversiveness, and sensory enjoyment, and which are mediated through nicotine and non-nicotine elements of smoking.

pmc-11728777.title: Synthesis and Characterization of Two Sparfloxacin Crystalline Salts: Enhancing Solubility and In Vitro Antibacterial Activity of Sparfloxacin
pmc-11728777.creator: Wei Sun, Ruili Huo, Jingzhong Duan, Jixiang Xiao, Yan Wang, Xiaoping Zhou, Clive Prestidge
pmc-11728777.description: Background: To improve the solubility and permeability of Sparfloxacin (SPX) and enhance its antimicrobial activity in vitro, two unreported pharmaceutical crystalline salts were synthesized and characterized in this paper. One is a hydrated crystal of Sparfloxacin with Pimelic acid (PIA), another is a hydrated crystal of Sparfloxacin with Azelaic acid (AZA), namely, SPX-PIA-H2O (2C19H23F2N4O3·C7H10O4·2H2O) and SPX-AZA-H2O (4C19H23F2N4O3·2C9H14O4·5H2O).

pmc-12838811.title: Phosvitin-Derived Peptide Pt5-1c Is a Pro-Angiogenic Agent Capable of Enhancing Wound Healing
pmc-12838811.creator: Cuiling Xuan, Mei Li, Peng Zhang, Yunchao Wang, Hongyan Li, Zhiqin Gao, Shicui Zhang, Fei Wu
pmc-12838811.description: Antimicrobial peptides (AMPs) have been shown to have pro-angiogenic activity, capable of enhancing neovascularization and facilitating the healing of chronic wounds. However, information as such remains rather limited. Here we clearly showed that the fish phosvitin-derived AMP Pt5-1c was able to enhance angiogenesis in both murine full-thickness wound models and zebrafish with vascular defects models.

pmc-13219642.title: Identification of physiological clusters in acute hypoxemic respiratory failure patients undergoing non-invasive respiratory support using EIT-based t-SNE and spectral clustering
pmc-13219642.creator: Gaetano Scaramuzzo, Valentina Bellini, Matteo Trevisani, Francesca Cinquegrana, Marta Bonanni, Marta Ciniero, Matteo Riccardo, Pierluigi Ferrara, Alessandro Trentini, Tiziana Bellini, Giulia Tini, Sara Uboldi, Danila Azzolina, Savino Spadaro, Carlo Alberto Volta, Elena Giovanna Bignami
pmc-13219642.description: PurposeIdentifying physiological clusters in acute hypoxemic respiratory failure (AHRF) may help to personalize non-invasive respiratory support (NIRS). Electrical impedance tomography (EIT) provides real-time, regional information on tidal ventilation, but its value for clustering AHRF patients undergoing NIRS has not been established.MethodsWe conducted a single-center observational study including adults with AHRF monitored with EIT during NIRS.

pmc-13246651.title: Atherogenic index of plasma and severe headaches or migraines risk in US adults: a population-based cross-sectional analysis from NHANES 1999–2004
pmc-13246651.creator: Shaoxiong Chen, Yi He, Jiaheng Xu
pmc-13246651.description: BackgroundDespite the established link between the atherogenic index of plasma (AIP) and cardiometabolic diseases, its association with severe headaches or migraines remains poorly characterized. This study aimed to explore the association between AIP and severe headaches or migraines using data from the National Health and Nutrition Examination Survey (NHANES).MethodsData were drawn from the NHANES 1999–2004, comprising 6,017 adults.

pmc-13376826.creator: Charles Gadd, Krishna Gokhale, Aditya Acharya, Jennifer Cooper, Francesca Crowe, Leah Fitzsimmons, Thomas Jackson, Krishnarajah Nirantharakumar, Christopher Yau, The OPTIMAL Consortium
pmc-13376826.description: Multiple long-term conditions (MLTCs), or multimorbidity—the co-occurrence of multiple chronic conditions—present a growing challenge for primary care. Existing predictive models typically focus on single outcomes and often fail to capture the temporal and competing-risk structure inherent in longitudinal electronic health records (EHRs). Here, we present SurvivEHR, a generative transformer-based foundation model trained on over 7.

pmc-13426215.title: Neuroendocrine transformation of prostate adenocarcinoma with liver and brain metastases: case report and literature review
pmc-13426215.creator: Luiz Carlos de Araújo Souza, Fernando Victor do Carmo, João Paulo Majella de Godoy Morais, Herbeth Franco Queiroz, Fábio Henrique Mendonça de Oliveira, Pedro Simões Daher
pmc-13426215.description: Treatment-emergent neuroendocrine prostate cancer (t-NEPC) is a rare and aggressive variant associated with resistance to androgen deprivation therapy and visceral metastases. We report a case of neuroendocrine transformation of metastatic prostate adenocarcinoma with liver and brain involvement. Diagnosis was confirmed by liver biopsy demonstrating neuroendocrine differentiation and a Ki-67 index of 95%. A literature review identified seven similar cases.
